findings.title: probeMonitor() is completely untested — all monitor tests are tautological
findings.description: The serve-mcp-monitor.test.ts tests bypass actual probeMonitor() execution entirely. They inject a mock handleToolCall that returns a hardcoded readiness object, then assert the value that was just injected comes back out. The real production logic — fetch with AbortSignal.timeout(200ms), resp.status < 500 check, 15-second cache TTL, cache expiry on subsequent calls, Map<string, MonitorProbeEntry> state — is never touched by any test. This is the most critical gap given probeMonitor() is called on every get_current_context invocation.
findings.evidence: packages/cli/src/index.ts lines 589-602: probeMonitor() contains fetch, AbortSignal.timeout, cache TTL logic. serve-mcp-monitor.test.ts line 33: handler always returns hardcoded monitor_running regardless of actual fetch behavior.
missing_scenarios: Cache hit: second call within TTL_MS should not re-fetch (assert fetch called once)
Cache expiry: call after TTL_MS should re-fetch
fetch returns 500 -> monitor_running = false (resp.status < 500 is false)
fetch returns 404 -> monitor_running = true (status < 500 is true — may be surprising)
findings.suggested_fix: Export probeMonitor() for testing or use vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...) to intercept. Use vi.useFakeTimers() / vi.setSystemTime() to advance past MONITOR_PROBE_TTL_MS (15000ms) for cache expiry tests. Reset _monitorProbeCache between tests via module reset or an exported clearProbeCache() helper.

findings.title: _monitorStarted double-start prevention is untested
findings.description: runServeAll() sets _monitorStarted = true then calls runServeMcp(). Inside runServeMcp(), the guard `if (!NO_MONITOR && !_monitorStarted)` prevents spawning a second monitor process. No test exercises this guard. If the flag ever breaks, two monitor instances would race for port 4721 at runtime, which is a silent correctness failure that only surfaces in production.
findings.evidence: packages/cli/src/index.ts lines 1272-1290: runServeAll sets _monitorStarted = true at line 1287, then calls runServeMcp() at line 1290. Line 1058: guard `if (!NO_MONITOR && !_monitorStarted)` in runServeMcp().
missing_scenarios: When runServeAll() has already set _monitorStarted=true, runServeMcp() must not spawn a second monitor
findings.suggested_fix: Export or expose _monitorStarted for reset between tests. Test by calling runServeMcp() after manually setting _monitorStarted=true and asserting no second monitor spawn occurs (mock startMonitorServer and verify it is called at most once across the combined runServeAll + runServeMcp flow).

findings.title: bin entry test asserts index.ts — brittle for npm publish
findings.description: The test at line 20 checks `bin['fulcrum-mcp']` contains 'index.ts'. The current package.json has `./src/index.ts` as the bin entry, which works with tsx at runtime. However, if the publish pipeline adds a build step that compiles to dist/index.js and updates the bin entry, this test would fail a legitimate publish — or worse, a publish to npm with the .ts bin entry breaks in consumers who lack tsx. The assertion conflates 'this value exists' with 'this specific runtime strategy is correct'.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert that the bin entry is defined and points to a file that exists on disk: `expect(existsSync(resolve(pkgDir, bin['fulcrum-mcp']))).toBe(true)`. If the publish strategy of shipping .ts with tsx shebang is intentional, add a comment documenting this decision so future maintainers don't change it unknowingly.

findings.title: fulcrum-mcp argv injection behavior is untested
findings.description: The fulcrum-mcp package's only meaningful logic is `process.argv.splice(2, 0, 'serve', 'mcp')` followed by `await import('@fulcrum/cli')`. The test file only validates package.json fields (name, bin, dependencies, engines). The actual delegation mechanism — that invoking `fulcrum-mcp` causes the CLI to enter MCP stdio mode — has zero test coverage. A typo in the splice call or a change to @fulcrum/cli's dispatch table would go undetected.
findings.evidence: packages/fulcrum-mcp/src/index.ts lines 29-32: the entire runtime behavior. index.test.ts lines 13-57: all tests read package.json, none exercise the module.
missing_scenarios: Spawning the fulcrum-mcp binary (or running index.ts directly) should produce MCP stdio output, not a help/error message
With --no-monitor flag, monitor should not auto-start
findings.suggested_fix: Add a spawnSync test that runs `node --import tsx/esm packages/fulcrum-mcp/src/index.ts` with a synthetic MCP initialize message on stdin and asserts the response looks like a valid MCP response (or at minimum that stderr doesn't contain 'Unknown command'). Keep timeout short (5s) with stdio pipe.

findings.title: install-checkpoint assertions are string-fragile and not behavior-anchored
findings.description: All assertions use toContain() on stdout with literal strings ('Doctor gate', 'bypassed', 'dry-run', 'seed'). Any log message rewording silently passes the behavior while breaking the test, or vice versa. The env-var bypass test (describe block at line 60) duplicates the --no-doctor-gate test: both exercise the same `NO_DOCTOR_GATE` branch of `runDoctorGate()` and assert identical output. Neither tests distinct behavior.
findings.evidence: install-checkpoint.test.ts lines 36-77. agent-integration/install.ts line 895: `NO_DOCTOR_GATE` is set once at module load from both env var and flag — both paths hit the same `skip()` call at line 899.
missing_scenarios: Exit code should be 0 for successful dry-run (currently not asserted)
stderr should be empty or contain only known warnings in dry-run mode
findings.suggested_fix: Add `expect(status).toBe(0)` assertions. Consider anchoring on machine-readable dry-run markers rather than human-readable strings, or add a --json output mode to install.ts.

findings.title: runDoctorGate() failure path (JSON parse, fail counts) is untested
findings.description: runDoctorGate() has three distinct non-bypass outcomes: (a) fulcrum not in PATH -> warn and return, (b) DRY_RUN -> dry log and ok, (c) live run -> parse JSON, count failures, call fail() or ok(). Only the bypass (env + flag) and partial dry-run paths are tested. The JSON-parse-failure branch and the failures.length > 0 branch that calls fail() are not covered.
findings.evidence: agent-integration/install.ts lines 897-944. install-checkpoint.test.ts lines 35-77: no test for actual doctor run outcomes.
findings.suggested_fix: These would need to mock the `fulcrum doctor --json` subprocess. Consider extracting the doctor result parsing into a pure function `parseDoctorOutput(stdout: string): DoctorResult` that can be unit tested directly without subprocess.

findings.title: regenerateClaudeMd() step in install.ts plan is untested
findings.description: The install plan (lines 853, 869 in install.ts) includes `['Regenerate CLAUDE.md from TOOL_SCHEMAS', regenerateClaudeMd]` as a step. install-checkpoint.test.ts has no test that verifies this step runs or produces expected output in dry-run mode. The gen-claude-md.test.ts covers the pure splice helpers but not the orchestration in install.ts's regenerateClaudeMd() function.
findings.evidence: agent-integration/install.ts lines 386-410, 853, 869. No corresponding test in install-checkpoint.test.ts.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a dry-run test that checks for 'Regenerate CLAUDE.md' in stdout, similar to the seed data test.

findings.title: FULCRUM_MONITOR_PORT test is also tautological — tests mock not production code
findings.description: The FULCRUM_MONITOR_PORT test (lines 87-130) sets process.env['FULCRUM_MONITOR_PORT'] = '9999' in beforeEach, then passes a handler that reads the env var and constructs the expectedUrl itself. The assertion `expect(readiness['monitor_url']).toBe('http://localhost:9999')` merely proves the mock read the env var correctly — it does not test that the production probeMonitor() or get_current_context handler reads FULCRUM_MONITOR_PORT. If the production code stopped reading this env var, the test would still pass.
findings.evidence: serve-mcp-monitor.test.ts lines 88-129: the handler at line 106 constructs `monitor_url: expectedUrl` where expectedUrl was built from the env var in the test itself, not from production code.
findings.suggested_fix: The test needs to use the real CLI handler (not a mock) and assert that its output reflects the env var. This requires integration-style testing against the real runServeMcp handler, or extracting a testable getMonitorUrl() helper from index.ts.

findings.title: spliceToolCount always writes 'tools' (plural) — count=1 produces '1 tools'
findings.description: The source at line 62 always formats as `exposes ${toolCount} tools` regardless of toolCount value. When toolCount === 1 this produces '1 tools'. No test catches this. The spliceToolCount test suite tests counts 42, 10, 27, 1 — but line 84 tests count=42, line 77 tests count=10 for idempotency, and none of the surrounding assertions check the singular form for count=1.
findings.evidence: scripts/gen-claude-md.ts line 62: `The \`fulcrum\` MCP server exposes ${toolCount} tools for...`. gen-claude-md.test.ts line 84 tests count=42 only.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the source: `exposes ${toolCount} tool${toolCount === 1 ? '' : 's'}`. Add test: `expect(spliceToolCount(original, 1)).toContain('exposes 1 tool')` and `expect(spliceToolCount(original, 1)).not.toContain('1 tools')`.

findings.title: spliceSection partial-marker edge case (one marker present, other absent) not tested
findings.description: spliceSection() checks for both START_MARKER and END_MARKER presence with `startIdx === -1 || endIdx === -1`. If only one marker is present, it falls through to the append path, which may produce malformed output with duplicate or unbalanced markers. This edge case isn't tested, though it is an implicit behavior contract.
findings.evidence: scripts/gen-claude-md.ts lines 45-47: append path triggered when either marker absent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add test: input with only START_MARKER but not END_MARKER should produce valid output with both markers. Alternatively, the function could throw on this case rather than silently produce potentially malformed output.

residual_risks.description: probeMonitor() runs on every get_current_context call in production. The 200ms AbortSignal timeout has never been exercised in tests. If fetch hangs for exactly 200ms-ish in a slow environment, the behavior (timeout fires, running=false, cache writes false) is untested and could mask a legitimate monitor that's slow to respond.

install.ts sets NO_DOCTOR_GATE at module load time (line 894-895). In the install-checkpoint tests, both bypass paths (env var and --no-doctor-gate) hit the same module-level constant. If install.ts is refactored to check argv/env at function call time instead, current tests would still pass even if the bypass broke — they don't isolate the two bypass mechanisms.

The fulcrum-mcp package ships a .ts file as its bin entry (./src/index.ts). This works with npx because tsx is listed as a dependency. If a consumer has npm@10+ with strict bin validation, or if the package is installed in an environment without tsx, the binary silently fails. No test validates the npx execution path end-to-end.

testing_gaps.description: The entire fetch+cache logic of probeMonitor() is untested. Needs: vi.stubGlobal('fetch'), vi.useFakeTimers(), and Map reset between tests. Should cover: cache hit, cache miss after TTL, fetch rejection, HTTP 200, HTTP 500, AbortSignal timeout.
No test verifies that runServeAll() -> runServeMcp() does not spawn two monitor processes. Requires mocking startMonitorServer and verifying call count.
The only runtime behavior of the package is untested. A spawn test using spawnSync with a synthetic MCP initialize payload on stdin would cover this.
The JSON parse failure, fail-count>0, and fulcrum-not-in-PATH branches of runDoctorGate() are untested. Would benefit from extracting parseDoctorOutput() as a testable pure function.
No dry-run test verifies this step appears/runs in the install plan.
count=1 produces '1 tools'. Minor bug in source + missing test.
